observation.visible_scene: Close-up of the back of a fair-skinned hand against a dark gray textured background, four fingers extending upward and a thumb at lower right, all with long manicured nails (nude base with pale/white tips). A solitaire ring with a large round brilliant-cut clear stone set in four prongs on a thin pale-metal band is worn on the second finger from the left (ring finger).
visible_changes: The gemstone's internal reflections and surface sparkle change continuously from frame to frame: bright white flashes and small colored 'fire' points (yellow, blue) appear at different facets (e.g., top-right in frame 4, bottom-left in frame 11, bottom in frame 31, left in frame 35), indicating a shifting light-to-stone angle.

The hand undergoes a subtle overall drift/tilt: comparing the first and last frames the ring shifts slightly up and to the right within the frame, and more of the band's left side becomes visible as a dark reflective surface in the later frames, consistent with a small rotation of the finger/hand rather than the ring moving on its own.
The thumb at lower right changes angle slightly across the sequence (nail orientation and position shift a little), matching a gentle repositioning of the whole hand.
The dark background and the hand's general framing remain otherwise constant throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the hand is being held, posed, or moved by an unseen person.
The cause of the changing sparkle (hand micro-rotation vs. a moving light source) and any motion before the first frame or after the last frame.
The exact material identity of the stone and band.
uncertain_details: The small positional drift of the hand/ring could be partly hand movement or partly camera movement; background texture is too uniform to confirm camera motion.
The sparkle changes are reflections on a single stone, not separate objects or a deformation of the stone.
